'''Jane Elizabeth Parker''' {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} (born 1960) is a British scientist who researches the immune responses of plants at the [[Max Planck Institute for Plant Breeding Research]].

==Education and early life==
Jane Elizabeth Parker was born in 1960 in Great Britain<ref name="Sofja Kovalevskaja Award 2002">{{cite web|title=Sofja Kovalevskaja Award 2002 – Award Winners (K-R)|url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/web/skp-2002-K-R-en.html|publisher=Humboldt Foundation|access-date=4 November 2015|location=Bonn, Germany|language=German|year=2002|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160426064721/https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/web/skp-2002-K-R-en.html|archive-date=26 April 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> and completed her undergraduate degree at the [[University of Bradford]] in applied [[Biology]] in 1983. She went on to earn her PhD in 1986 from [[Swansea University]] on [[protein synthesis]] in ''[[Euglena]]''.<ref>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University College of Swansea|title=Developmental regulation of protein synthesis in Euglena gracilis|first= Jane Elizabeth|last=Parker|year=1987|url=http://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.638412|oclc=502374732}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Following her PhD, she was a [[postdoctoral researcher]] at the [[Max Planck Institute for Plant Breeding Research]].<ref name="Leopoldina bio">{{cite web|title=Curriculum Vitae Prof. Dr. Jane Parker|url=http://www.leopoldina.org/fileadmin/redaktion/Mitglieder/CV_Parker-Jane_ENG.pdf|publisher=Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften Leopoldina|access-date=4 November 2015|location=Halle, Germany|year=2013}}</ref> Throughout the 1990s, she worked at the [[Sainsbury Laboratory]] at the John Innes Centre in the Norwich Research Park, at [[Norwich]], England, but left in August 2001, with her husband, Dr. [[George Coupland]] to take up a post as an independent researcher at [[Cologne]]'s [[Max Planck Institute]].{{sfn|John Innes Centre|2001|p=41}}

In 2002, Parker was awarded a [[Sofia Kovalevskaya Award]] to continue her research into plant immune responses. She researches how plants defend themselves from disease-causing [[microorganism]]s. Her work involves isolating the genes which trigger innate defence mechanisms and combines genetics with molecular biology to evaluate how plants are able to avoid disease.<ref name="Sofja Kovalevskaja Award 2002" /> Her research has discovered that there are multiple layers of defence but that a protein, called EDS1, which combines with other proteins to form complexes, is the initial trigger. The immune response varies depending on whether the complex formed is developed from combining with the protein PAD4 or SAG101 to initiate the response to disease resistance.<ref name="Phys dot org">{{cite news|title=Molecular snapshot of the plant immune system's signal box|url=http://phys.org/news/2013-12-molecular-snapshot-immune.html|access-date=4 November 2015|publisher=Phys.org|date=12 December 2013|location=Douglas, Isle of Man, United Kingdom}}</ref>

Since 2009, Parker has been an associate professor at the [[Institute of Genetics University of Cologne]] in Germany.<ref name="Leopoldina bio" /> In 2013, she was elected a member of the [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]],<ref>{{cite web|title=List of Members: Prof. Dr. Jane Parker|url=http://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/member/7721/|publisher=Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften Leopoldina|access-date=5 November 2015|location=Halle, Germany|year=2013}}</ref> and in 2023 she was elected an international member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ravindran |first=Sandeep |date=2025-11-19 |title=QnAs with Jane E. Parker |url=https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2530986122 |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America |volume=122 |issue=48 |doi=10.1073/PNAS.2530986122|doi-access=free }}</ref> She is widely published and has been listed on the annual [[ISI Web of Knowledge]] most highly cited scientists for 2015, as published by Thomson Reuters.<ref name="Highly Cited">{{cite web|title=Highly Cited Researchers 2015|url=http://highlycited.com/|access-date=4 November 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.mpipz.mpg.de/23590/curriculum_vitae |title = Curriculum Vitae}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
She is listed on [[Thomson Reuters]]' list of the annual [[ISI Web of Knowledge]] most highly cited scientists for 2015.<ref>{{cite book |ref={{harvid|John Innes Centre|2001}}|title=John Innes Centre & Sainsbury Laboratory Annual Report 2001|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=OSTbAAAAMAAJ|year=2001|publisher=The Centre|location=Norwich, England |page=41}}</ref> She was elected a member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] in 2016<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://people.embo.org/profile/jane-e-parker |title = Find people in the EMBO Communities}}</ref> and a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jane Parker |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/jane-parker-36235/ |access-date=2023-05-24 |website=royalsociety.org}}</ref>
